tweets.text: This is like AI slop it literally says nothing? Did Megaspeed violate laws or not? https://t.co/SnFyxhyIBw

My top 5 takeaways from @nateparrott on how to get Claude to design without AI slop:

1. Give Claude context upfront.

Share screenshots, pages you like, and your past work. For an existing product, have Claude rebuild the real screens from code.

2. Research familiar UX patterns.

For hard layout problems, ask Claude to research familiar products that solve something similar and note the layouts people already know how to use.

3. Make Claude aware of its design biases.

"The model has no idea what its own biases are." In your design.md or another file, consider discouraging Claude's tells like serif text, off-white backgrounds, and card-edge bars.

4. Start with wireframes.

Have Claude create wireframes first and give it feedback to nail your core user flows before going deep on fonts and colors.

5. Ask for multiple options, then remix them.

Ask Claude for 5 options for key screens with different fonts, colors, and styles. Then pick the parts you like and ask it to remix and create 5 more options.

📌 Watch the full episode now: https://t.co/HPX5HjXafX

Also available as a written post: https://t.co/jcofmkQc01
tweets.summary_en: To get less generic designs from Claude, provide visual context, research familiar UX patterns, explicitly discourage its design clichés, and refine user flows through wireframes before styling. Generate multiple design options, then remix the strongest elements iteratively.

builders.name: Aaron Levie
builders.summary_en: Observes continued growth in token spending per employee and argues that AI usage and adoption are still early in their expansion.
builders.summary_zh: 观察到人均 token 支出持续增长，并认为 AI 使用量和普及程度仍处于扩张早期。

slang.definition_en: Spending on model usage measured through units of text or other content processed or generated.
slang.definition_zh: 按模型处理或生成的文本等内容单位计算的使用支出。

keywords.definition_zh: 指平均每位员工使用 AI token 所产生的支出。
keywords.example_zh: 作者用人均 token 支出持续上升的现象，表达自己对 AI 使用和普及仍处早期阶段的判断。

keywords.definition_zh: 指暂时看不到增长的上限。
keywords.example_zh: 这里形容人均 token 支出的增长趋势尚未显露触顶迹象，并非证明它可以无限增长。

tweets.text:
The chart of token spend per employee still has no ceiling in sight. And the closer you are to AI right now the deeper the sense is that we’re actually still in the early part of the curve of token use and adoption. 

This summer and fall’s model releases have continued to push the state of the art forward at a rate that already felt hard to maintain. As a result, for most productive use-cases the models are only now starting to actually work, and the feeling is that things will only accelerate from here.

Coding, in retrospect, was basically trash even 12 months ago. Now it’s finally starting to get good. And now that coding is actually working, you’re getting tool and computer use, which open up a wide variety of knowledge work domains that weren’t possible to throw agents at before.

Once you have agents that can code, use computers, leverage any tool out there, and understand a variety of domains, you can begin to throw them at a wide variety of knowledge work tasks that were hard to bring automation to across finance, life sciences, cyber, and more. So that brings agents to a broad set of work that we’re not really using them in yet at scale. 

Then comes the new form factors of agents. Agent swarms and background agents are going to eat up vastly more tokens than anything we can imagine. You’ll have agents running in most enterprises workflows processing data, validating work, doing research, providing decision support, and so on. And we’ll have swarms that fan out in parallel in areas like cyber, life sciences, coding, and more.

So basically tokens are only going up from here.
tweets.summary_en: AI token consumption is likely to keep rising as improving coding, tool use, and computer use make agents practical across more knowledge work. Background agents and parallel swarms could multiply demand as enterprises deploy them for research, validation, data processing, and decision support.

vocab.example_en: This typeface has a small serif at the end of each main stroke.
vocab.example_zh: 这种字体的每个主要笔画末端都有一小段衬线。

vocab.definition_en: A revealing sign that gives away something's origin or someone's hidden state.
vocab.definition_zh: 暴露来源或隐藏状态的迹象；破绽
vocab.example_en: The repeated decorative bars became a tell of AI-generated design.
vocab.example_zh: 反复出现的装饰条成了暴露 AI 生成设计的明显迹象。

vocab.definition_en: An important idea or lesson to remember from something.
vocab.definition_zh: 要点；值得记住的收获或启示
vocab.example_en: My biggest takeaway was to test the user flow early.
vocab.example_zh: 我最大的收获是要尽早测试用户操作流程。

vocab.definition_en: Allowing users to take actions and receive responses.
vocab.definition_zh: 交互式的；允许用户操作并获得反馈的
vocab.example_en: They turned their research sources into an interactive site.
vocab.example_zh: 他们把研究资料转化成了一个交互式网站。

quote.text_en: Build something small, learn from it, and make the next version better.
quote.text_zh: 先做出一个小成果，从中学习，再让下一个版本更好。
quote.author: Original quote

slang_glossary.definition_en: A derogatory term for low-quality, generic, or meaningless AI-generated content.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 对低质量、套路化或言之无物的 AI 生成内容的贬称。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A system that organizes and automates software production, increasingly using AI agents.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 将软件生产流程系统化、自动化的体系，如今常包含 AI 智能体。

slang_glossary.definition_en: AI systems that pursue tasks by taking steps and using tools with some autonomy.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 能够自主执行步骤、调用工具并推进任务的 AI 智能体。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The surrounding software that runs, controls, equips, or evaluates a model or agent.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 用于运行、控制、配置或评估模型及智能体的外围软件框架。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Zero Data Retention, a policy under which a provider does not retain specified customer data after processing, subject to its terms.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: Zero Data Retention 的缩写，即零数据保留，具体涵盖的数据和条件取决于服务条款。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Short for evaluations, meaning tests used to measure model or agent performance.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: evaluations 的简称，指衡量模型或智能体表现的评测。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Running model predictions or generation with protections for the privacy of inputs and outputs.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在保护输入和输出隐私的条件下执行模型推理或生成。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The volume or cost of tokens consumed while using AI models.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 使用 AI 模型时消耗的 token 数量或相应费用。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Numerical vector representations that encode useful properties or relationships of data.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 将数据的特征或关系编码为数值向量的表示，常用于语义搜索和相似度计算。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal name for a shared knowledge system that makes a company's information accessible, often through AI.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 对企业共享知识系统的形象说法，通常借助 AI 组织和检索公司信息。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal approach to building software by prompting AI and iterating on its output, often with limited inspection of the code.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 通过自然语言指挥 AI 写代码并持续试改的开发方式，使用者往往较少深入检查代码。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Isolated environments for running code with controlled access to other resources.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 沙箱；用于执行代码并限制其访问其他资源的隔离环境。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Continuous integration workflows in which AI agents perform tasks such as investigating failures or proposing fixes.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 引入 AI 智能体执行故障调查、提出修复方案等任务的持续集成流程。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An expression of sympathy and support for operations teams handling outages or incidents.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 向正在处理宕机或事故的运维团队表达理解和支持的网络用语。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Informally, repeatedly supervising a system and intervening to keep it working.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在技术语境中指反复盯着系统运行，并不断介入处理问题。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Depending on context, visible evidence of completed effort or a blockchain mechanism requiring computational work.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 可指证明实际付出或成果的材料，也可指区块链中的工作量证明机制，含义取决于上下文。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Units into which a model divides text or other inputs and outputs for processing.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 模型处理输入和输出时使用的基本单位，文本 token 可以是一个字、词或词的一部分。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Technology businesses centered on substantial physical engineering, hardware, or scientific development.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 以实体工程、硬件或科学研发为核心，通常需要较长研发周期的硬科技。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Working near the hardware level, with attention to chip behavior and low-level performance.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 贴近芯片和硬件底层开展工作，关注底层机制与性能。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A vulgar abbreviation of what the fuck, expressing shock, confusion, or anger.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: what the fuck 的粗俗缩写，用来表达震惊、困惑或愤怒。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A texting abbreviation for right now.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: right now 的聊天缩写，意为「现在」或「此刻」。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal abbreviation for Google Calendar.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: Google Calendar，即谷歌日历的非正式简称。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal shortening of calendar, sometimes referring to a calendar event or invitation.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: calendar 的非正式简写，有时也指日历事项或会议邀请。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Established interaction and interface solutions that users recognize from other products.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 用户在其他产品中已经熟悉的交互与界面设计模式，UX 是用户体验的缩写。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Simplified interface sketches used to plan structure before detailed visual styling.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 线框图；在细化视觉样式之前规划界面结构的简化草图。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The sequences of steps users take to complete tasks in a product.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 用户在产品中完成某项任务所经历的一系列操作步骤。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Recognizable signs that reveal a creator, source, or recurring tendency.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 能够暴露创作者、来源或惯常倾向的特征；文中指容易辨认的 AI 设计痕迹。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Text set in a typeface with small finishing strokes on its letters.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 使用衬线字体排版的文字，字母主要笔画末端带有小装饰笔画。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Decorative or functional strips placed along the edges of interface cards.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 放在界面卡片边缘、起装饰或提示作用的条形元素。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Informally, to execute or get something exactly right.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 口语中指把某件事做好、做准或做到位。
